How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Every node is one actual sticker, in one solid color. Connected rings show the sticker paths for every rotation axis. The selected axis stays bright while the other rings remain visible. Click any ring to select it, then drag along its path to turn. “Focus selected rings” dims the other axes without removing them.

Main U, L, R, B turns rotate two layers including the tip; wide Uw, Lw, Rw, Bw turns rotate three layers; lowercase u, l, r, b rotate one tip. All turns are 120°. Each solved face has 16 triangular stickers, shown as one circular node per sticker. Select a layer from its row, then drag a ring or use the direction buttons. Keyboard U L R B turns the main layer; Alt selects wide turns and Shift reverses either. Use the tip buttons for individual tips. Click a colored dot to inspect its piece’s home, current position, and full orientation.

Drag the 3D puzzle to look around; scroll or pinch to zoom. Click a visible axis letter to select it. With the 3D view focused, arrows rotate the camera and +/− zoom. The animation slider controls every move, including randomizing and auto solving, and can be changed while a sequence is running.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies legal moves using a fresh seed. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. Stop exits Auto Solve at the next completed stage, or cancels an unfinished scramble turn; Reset returns to solved. The built-in solution guide explains how to solve by hand. State stays in this browser tab.
